podcast.title: Additional Musical Projects
podcast.body: Beyond her work with Sleater-Kinney, Brownstein has been involved in other musical projects, including contributing to soundtracks and participating in other bands. "Oh, and there's been more music too, including some soundtracks and a couple of bands outside of Slider Kinney."

podcast.title: Early Guitar Learning
podcast.body: Carrie Brownstein began taking guitar lessons at age 15, with her first guitar being the inaugural item she saved up for and bought entirely by herself. "She started taking guitar lessons at age 15. Her first guitar was the first thing she ever had to save up for and pay for by herself."

podcast.body: During the band's initial period, Carrie Brownstein gained considerable notice for her guitar playing, even being specifically highlighted by Rolling Stone magazine. "During the first go around, Kerry got quite a bit of notice for her guitar playing. She was even singled up by Rolling Stone."

podcast.title: Multi-faceted Career
podcast.body: In addition to her musical endeavors, Carrie Brownstein is also a writer, blogger, and actor. She is known for co-starring with Fred Armisen in the show "Portlandia," playing the role of Sid in "Transparent," appearing on "Curb Your Enthusiasm," and providing voice work for "Archer" and "The Simpsons." "She's also a writer, a blogger, and an actor. She's done really well with the show Portlandia, co-starring Fred Armiston. She played the role of Sid in the series Transparent. You might have seen her on Curb Your Enthusiasm, and she's been a voice on both Archer and The Simpsons."

podcast.title: Post-Sleater-Kinney Career
podcast.body: After her time in Sleater-Kinney, Carrie Brownstein expanded her career into writing and acting. She wrote for and appeared on *Saturday Night Live* and co-created, wrote for, and starred in the Emmy-winning series *Portlandia* with Fred Armisen. She has also made appearances in *Curb Your Enthusiasm*, *Archer*, *The Simpsons*, and *Transparent*. "She later went on to write for an appearance Saturday Night Live. Maybe you've seen the Emmy award winning series she did with Fred Armason called Portlandia."

xref.title: Origins and History
xref.body: A trio of women from Olympia, Washington, Sleater-Kinney became prominent within the Riot Girl indie rock scene. The band formed while Carrie Brownstein was at university, remained active for approximately twelve years, broke up in 2006, and then reformed in 2014. "a trio of women out of Olympia, Washington. ... Peter Kinney came about while she was at university. They stuck it out for about a dozen years, broke up in 2006, and then reformed in 2014."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Second Wave Post-Riot Grrrl Band
xref.body: Sleater-Kinney was formed in Olympia around 1994 by Corin Tucker (formerly of Heavens to Betsy) and Carrie Brownstein. While not "exactly Riot Girls," they were deeply influenced by the movement and continued its feminist, left-leaning political messages, becoming a fixture on the American indie scene for about 10 years after the original Riot Grrrl scene faded. "One of them was Slater Kinney featuring current Tucker of Evans De Betsy and Carrie Brown Steen."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
